label: As casus belli
summary: Going by its name, the stored script object read as a casus belli (a war's reason and goal).
details: Scope is the general holder for a script object, the kind that MakeScope makes and Var('name') hands back; functions like this one read it as one particular kind of thing. Vanilla never uses this one. The game documents no return type.

label: As character
summary: The stored script object read as a character.
details: Scope is the general holder for a script object: MakeScope makes one, Var('name') hands back the object saved in a variable, and the items of a MakeScope.GetList list are such holders. Vanilla uses Char to turn them into a character for portraits and name texts, for example in the funeral selection list and the situation list, and as MakeScope.Var('stele_container').Char in texts.

label: As character memory
summary: The stored script object read as a character memory (a remembered event in a character's past).
details: Scope is the general holder for a script object, such as what Var('name') hands back. Vanilla's legend texts read a saved variable this way and then ask the memory for its description.

label: As combat
summary: Going by its name, the stored script object read as a combat (a battle in progress).
details: Scope is the general holder for a script object, such as what Var('name') hands back. Vanilla never names this function; the one line with the same word is plain tutorial text. The game documents no return type.

label: As combat side
summary: Going by its name, the stored script object read as one side of a combat.
details: Scope is the general holder for a script object, such as what Var('name') hands back. Vanilla never uses this one. The game documents no return type.

label: As confederation
summary: Going by its name, the stored script object read as a confederation (an alliance of realms).
details: Scope is the general holder for a script object, such as what Var('name') hands back. Vanilla never names this function; the lines with the same word are plain text. The game documents no return type.

label: As confederation type
summary: Going by its name, the stored script object read as a confederation type.
details: Scope is the general holder for a script object, such as what Var('name') hands back. Vanilla never uses this one. The game documents no return type.

label: As court position

details: Scope is the general holder for a script object, such as what Var('name') hands back. Vanilla never uses this one. The game documents no return type.

label: As court position type
summary: Going by its name, the stored script object read as a type of court position.
details: Scope is the general holder for a script object. Vanilla never names Scope.CourtPositionType; the tooltip lines that use the bare word belong to another context. The game documents no return type.

label: As culture

details: Scope is the general holder for a script object, such as what Var('name') hands back. Vanilla reads saved variables this way, for example MakeScope.Var('mend_the_fracture_oath_target_culture').Culture.GetName in the coronation texts.

label: As innovation
summary: The stored script object read as a culture innovation (an advance a culture can research).
details: Scope is the general holder for a script object, such as what Var('name') hands back. Vanilla reads a saved `innovation` variable this way to show its name.

details: Scope is the general holder for a script object, such as what Var('name') hands back. Vanilla never uses this one. The game documents no return type.

label: As culture tradition
summary: Going by its name, the stored script object read as a culture tradition.
details: Scope is the general holder for a script object, such as what Var('name') hands back. Vanilla never uses this one. The game documents no return type.

label: As decision
summary: Going by its name, the stored script object read as a decision type.
details: Scope is the general holder for a script object, such as what Var('name') hands back. Vanilla never uses this one. The game documents no return type.

details: Scope is the general holder for a script object, such as what Var('name') hands back. Vanilla's ecumenical council texts read saved debate proposals this way and show the doctrine's name.

label: As domicile
summary: Going by its name, the stored script object read as a domicile (a camp, estate or similar home).
details: Scope is the general holder for a script object, such as what Var('name') hands back. Vanilla never names this function; the one line with the same word is plain tutorial text. The game documents no return type.

summary: The stored script object read as a dynasty.
details: Scope is the general holder for a script object, such as what Var('name') hands back. Vanilla's memory texts read a saved `adopted_dynasty` variable this way to show the dynasty's name.

label: As epidemic
summary: The script object read as an epidemic (an outbreak of disease).
details: Vanilla's epidemic texts use ROOT.Epidemic and read the province where it first broke out, then that county's holder, top liege and primary title to name the realm and ruler. The game documents no return type.

label: As epidemic type
summary: Going by its name, the stored script object read as a kind of disease that spreads as epidemics.
details: Scope is the general holder for a script object, such as what Var('name') hands back. Vanilla never uses this one. The game documents no return type.

label: As faction
summary: The stored script object read as a faction (a group of vassals pushing a demand).
details: Scope is the general holder for a script object, such as what Var('name') hands back. Vanilla's task contract texts read a saved `task_contract_faction` variable this way to show the faction's name.

label: As faith
summary: The stored script object read as a faith.
details: Scope is the general holder for a script object, such as what Var('name') hands back. Vanilla reads saved variables this way, for example the faith a religious text artifact belongs to.

label: As region
summary: The stored script object read as a geographical region (a named group of provinces).
details: Scope is the general holder for a script object, such as what Var('name') hands back. Vanilla's natural disaster texts read a saved `river_region` variable this way to show the region's name.

label: Character
summary: The stored script object read as a character.
details: Scope is the general holder for a script object, such as what Var('name') hands back. Vanilla uses it as MakeScope.Var('wager_target').GetCharacter in the chariot race texts.

label: Flag key
summary: The key of the flag the script object holds, as text.
details: A flag is a plain word written as `flag:name`. Vanilla's one use reads a variable holding a flag, ROOT.Var('new_realm_title_name').GetFlagKey, in a text that set_title_name_dynamic uses to name a new realm title; the variable holds flags such as `flag:capital_duchy_name`.

label: Flag name
summary: The flag that the stored script object holds, shown as text.
details: A script object can be a plain flag (a word written as `flag:name`). Vanilla saves such flags in variables and prints them with MakeScope.Var('name').GetFlagName, for example the kind of animal in a contract scheme text or a compliment word in a task contract title. Going by those uses the flag is shown through localization; the game documents nothing more.

label: As title
summary: The stored script object read as a landed title.
details: Scope is the general holder for a script object, such as what Var('name') hands back. Vanilla reads the elector titles saved on the empire this way, for example MakeScope.Var('hre_elector_1').GetLandedTitle.GetNameNoTier.

label: Variable list
summary: The variable list with the given name on the stored script object, for showing its items.
details: Script keeps variable lists on objects (filled with add_to_variable_list). Vanilla GUI uses it as Activity.MakeScope.GetList('artifact_rewards') or GetPlayer.MakeScope.GetList('funeral_activity_targets') as a datamodel; each item is again a Scope, read with Char, Trait and so on.

fields.name: Arg0
fields.text: The name of the variable list.

label: As province
summary: The stored script object read as a province.
details: Scope is the general holder for a script object, such as what Var('name') hands back. Vanilla reads saved variables this way, for example the place a pilgrim badge artifact comes from.

label: As scheme
summary: The script object read as a scheme (a plot such as murder or seduction).
details: Vanilla texts use ROOT.GetScheme to read the scheme's name (the short label text SCOPE_SCHEME) or its owner, as in the learn language scheme texts that name the owner's court language. The global GetScheme('murder') is a different function. The game documents no return type.

label: Script value breakdown
summary: A text describing the script value named in brackets, worked out for the script object.
details: Vanilla's tournament aptitude tooltips use Character.MakeScope.GetScriptValueDesc('contest_type_aptitude_wit') and the like, and add it on a new line only when it is not empty. That the text is the value's breakdown rests on the name and this use.

label: Number
summary: The number that the stored script object holds.
details: A variable can hold a plain number instead of a character or title. Vanilla prints such numbers with MakeScope.Var('name').GetValue, for example a character's movement power or the chance to win a chariot race wager.

label: Number or default
summary: Going by its name, the number that the stored script object holds, or the given fallback number when it holds none.
details: It takes one argument, presumably the fallback. Vanilla never uses it, and the game documents nothing more.

fields.name: Arg0
fields.text: Going by the name, the number to use when there is no value.

label: Variable
summary: Going by its name, the variable with the given name on the stored script object, as a new script object.
details: It returns a Scope again, so the result can be read on (Char, GetValue and so on). The only similar lines are on situation history entries, a different type, and are a hint at most.

label: As government
summary: The stored script object read as a government type (feudal, clan, tribal and so on).
details: Scope is the general holder for a script object, such as what Var('name') hands back. Vanilla's memory texts read a saved `war_gov` variable this way to show the government's name, in the text of a war started to impose a government.

label: As great holy war
summary: The script object read as a great holy war (a crusade or similar faith-wide war).
details: Vanilla's one use is the short label text for a great holy war (SCOPE_GREAT_HOLY_WAR), ROOT.GreatHolyWar.GetName followed by a colon. The game documents no return type.

label: As great project
summary: Going by its name, the stored script object read as a great project (a large shared building work).
details: Scope is the general holder for a script object. The one line with the same name is a map icon's context and may belong to another type. The game documents no return type.

label: As project improvement
summary: Going by its name, the stored script object read as an improvement of a great project.
details: Scope is the general holder for a script object, such as what Var('name') hands back. Vanilla never uses this one. The game documents no return type.

label: Has flag
summary: Whether the stored script object has the flag with the given name.
details: Vanilla checks Scope.HasFlag('passed_provincial_exam') in the imperial examination text; the same name is a character flag in the examination activity's script (`has_character_flag`). The situation list also calls Story.MakeScope.HasFlag with a variable name from a story counter, so the name can be a variable's name there. The game documents nothing more.

fields.name: Arg0
fields.text: The name of the flag to look for.

label: As holy order
summary: The script object read as a holy order (a faith's military order).
details: Vanilla reads the holy order's name through it: in the short label text (ROOT.HolyOrder.GetName) and in the tooltip for reforming an order (THIS.HolyOrder.GetName). The game documents no return type.

label: As holy site
summary: The stored script object read as a holy site.
details: Scope is the general holder for a script object, such as what Var('name') hands back. Vanilla's travel planner text reads a saved `poi_standalone_holy_site` variable this way and checks whether it is an eminent holy site of a faith.

label: As holy site type
summary: Going by its name, the stored script object read as a holy site definition.
details: Scope is the general holder for a script object, such as what Var('name') hands back. Vanilla never uses this one. The game documents no return type.

label: As house
summary: The stored script object read as a dynasty house.
details: Scope is the general holder for a script object, such as what Var('name') hands back. Vanilla's interaction texts read a saved `petition_house_rights` variable this way to show the house's name.

label: As house relation
summary: Going by its name, the stored script object read as a relation between two dynasty houses.
details: Scope is the general holder for a script object, such as what Var('name') hands back. Vanilla never uses this one. The game documents no return type.

label: As inspiration
summary: The script object read as an inspiration (a character's urge to make an artifact or similar work).
details: Vanilla's one use is the short label text for an inspiration (SCOPE_INSPIRATION), ROOT.Inspiration.GetName. The game documents no return type.

label: Is set
summary: Whether the stored script object actually holds something.
details: Vanilla uses it to hide parts of the Christian church window when nothing is there, and as MakeScope.Var('first_debate_proposal').IsSet to check whether a variable was saved before showing it.

label: As legend
summary: The stored script object read as a legend (a story spread about a character).
details: Scope is the general holder for a script object, such as what Var('name') hands back. Vanilla's legend book texts read a saved `finished_legend_var` variable this way to show the legend's name, its chapter text and its protagonist.

label: As legend type
summary: Going by its name, the stored script object read as a type of legend.
details: Scope is the general holder for a script object, such as what Var('name') hands back. Vanilla never uses this one. The game documents no return type.

label: As mercenary company
summary: The script object read as a mercenary company.
details: Vanilla's one use is the short label text for a mercenary company (SCOPE_MERCENARY_COMPANY), ROOT.MercenaryCompany.GetName followed by a colon. The game documents no return type.

label: As organization
summary: Going by its name, the stored script object read as an organization.
details: Scope is the general holder for a script object, such as what Var('name') hands back. Vanilla never uses this one, and the game documents nothing about what an organization is here.

label: As province
summary: The stored script object read as a province.
details: Scope is the general holder for a script object, such as what Var('name') hands back. Vanilla reads saved variables this way, for example the province where an adventure artifact was found.

label: As regiment
summary: Going by its name, the stored script object read as a regiment of men-at-arms.
details: Scope is the general holder for a script object, such as what Var('name') hands back. Vanilla never names this function; the lines with the same word are plain text. The game documents no return type.

label: As religion
summary: The script object read as a religion (the family a faith belongs to).
details: Vanilla's one use is the short label text for a religion (SCOPE_RELIGION), ROOT.Religion.GetName followed by a colon. The game documents no return type.

label: As rite
summary: The stored script object read as a rite (a tradition of the Christian church, going by the church window).
details: Vanilla uses it in the Christian church window for the rite shown for each side of a schism, and as MakeScope.Var('schism_mainline_rite').Rite.GetName in its texts. That a rite is a church tradition rests on those uses; the game documents nothing more.

label: As rite type
summary: Going by its name, the stored script object read as a type of rite.
details: Scope is the general holder for a script object, such as what Var('name') hands back. Vanilla never uses this one. The game documents no return type.

label: As scheme
summary: Going by its name, the stored script object read as a scheme (a plot against someone).
details: Scope is the general holder for a script object, such as what Var('name') hands back. Vanilla never names this function; the lines with the same word are plain text. The game documents no return type.

label: Script value
summary: The result of the named script value, worked out for the stored script object.
details: Vanilla uses it in texts to print numbers, for example Scope.ScriptValue('fp3_house_modifier_concession_ending_duration') or GetPlayer.MakeScope.ScriptValue('sub_realm_size_value').

fields.name: Arg0
fields.text: The key of the script value to compute.
fields.values: a script value key in quotes

summary: Going by its name, the stored script object itself.
details: Vanilla never names it on this type. Self appears often after other types (for example Character.Self passed as an argument); those lines are only a hint. The game documents no return type.

summary: Going by its name, the stored script object read as a sub-region of a situation (one part of the map it covers).

label: As story
summary: Going by its name, the stored script object read as a story (a story cycle tied to a ruler).
details: Scope is the general holder for a script object, such as what Var('name') hands back. Vanilla never names this function; the lines with the same word are plain concept texts. The game documents no return type.

label: As struggle
summary: The stored script object read as a struggle (a long regional conflict).
details: Scope is the general holder for a script object, such as what Var('name') hands back. Vanilla's coronation texts read a saved `end_the_struggle_oath_type_var` variable this way to show the struggle's name.

label: As subject contract type
summary: Going by its name, the stored script object read as a type of subject contract (the terms between a liege and a subject).
details: Scope is the general holder for a script object, such as what Var('name') hands back. Vanilla never uses this one. The game documents no return type.

label: As task contract
summary: Going by its name, the stored script object read as a task contract (a job taken on by an adventurer or similar).
details: Scope is the general holder for a script object, such as what Var('name') hands back. Vanilla never uses this one. The game documents no return type.

label: As task contract type
summary: Going by its name, the stored script object read as a type of task contract.
details: Scope is the general holder for a script object, such as what Var('name') hands back. Vanilla never uses this one. The game documents no return type.

label: As tenet
summary: The stored script object read as a tenet (a core belief of a faith).
details: Scope is the general holder for a script object, such as what Var('name') hands back. Vanilla's ecumenical council event texts read a saved `current_topic` variable this way to show the tenet's name.

label: As title
summary: The stored script object read as a landed title.
details: Scope is the general holder for a script object, such as an item of a variable list or what Var('name') hands back. Vanilla uses it to show title coats of arms in the situation list, and as MakeScope.Var('administrative_ui_special_title').Title in greeting texts.

label: As trait
summary: The stored script object read as a trait.
details: Vanilla uses it on the items of an activity's `trait_rewards` variable list (Activity.MakeScope.GetList('trait_rewards')) to show each reward trait's icon.

label: As travel plan
summary: The script object read as a travel plan (a character's planned journey).
details: Vanilla's one use is the short label text for a travel plan (SCOPE_TRAVEL_PLAN), ROOT.TravelPlan.GetName followed by a colon. The game documents no return type.

label: Variable
summary: The value saved in the variable with the given name on the stored script object, as a new script object.
details: It returns a Scope again, so the result is then read as what it holds: Char, Title, GetValue, GetFlagName and so on. Vanilla uses it everywhere in texts, for example MakeScope.Var('stele_container').Char, and can chain it, as in MakeScope.Var('wager_target').Var('percent_chance_to_win').GetValue.

label: Variable time left
summary: The time left before the variable named in brackets runs out on the script object.
details: Vanilla uses it for cooldowns: it passes the result to GetGameTimeDifferenceForDiffDays, as in THIS.VarRemaining('isolating_cooldown_var') for "... remaining until you can Isolate again" and for court position recruitment cooldowns. So it suits variables set with a duration; going by that function's name, the number is in days.

label: As war
summary: The stored script object read as a war.
details: Scope is the general holder for a script object, such as what Var('name') hands back. Vanilla's task contract texts read a saved `task_contract_war` variable this way.

label: Access debug data itself
summary: A function on the scope debug data (an inspector entry of the debug tools) that, going by its name, hands back the entry itself.
details: Vanilla never names it on this type; PdxGuiWidget.AccessSelf is a different type and only a hint. The game documents no return type.

label: Debug information
summary: The debug text naming the script object the scope debug inspector is looking at.
details: Part of the engine's debug tools. The inspector shows it in bold as its heading, followed by the object's type name in brackets.

label: Raw ID
summary: The raw data or ID of the inspected script object, as text.
details: Part of the engine's debug tools; the scope debug inspector shows it in the row "Raw Data/ID:".

label: Type data
summary: The extra type data of the inspected script object, as text.
details: Part of the engine's debug tools; the scope debug inspector shows it in the row "Type Data:". The object editor describes type data as optional extra data that further sets a scope apart in a few cases.

label: Type ID
summary: The ID of the inspected script object's type, as text.
details: Part of the engine's debug tools; the scope debug inspector shows it in the row "Type ID:".

label: Type name
summary: The name of the inspected script object's type.
details: Part of the engine's debug tools; the scope debug inspector shows it in brackets after the object's debug text in its heading.

label: Is valid
summary: Whether the inspected script object is valid.
details: Part of the engine's debug tools; the scope debug inspector shows it as a read-only check box labelled "Is Valid:".

label: Debug data itself
summary: A function on the scope debug data that, going by its name, hands back the entry itself.
details: Vanilla never names it on this type. Self appears often after other types (for example Character.Self passed as an argument); those lines are only a hint. The game documents no return type.

label: Supports variables
summary: Whether the inspected script object can carry script variables.
details: Part of the engine's debug tools; the scope debug inspector shows it as a read-only check box labelled "Supports Variables:".

label: Access inspector itself
summary: A function on the scope inspector of the debug tools that, going by its name, hands back the inspector itself.
details: Vanilla never names it on this type; PdxGuiWidget.AccessSelf is a different type and only a hint. The game documents no return type.

label: Inspected object data
summary: The debug data of the script object the scope debug inspector is looking at.
details: Returns a ScopeDebugData; the inspector reads from it the debug text, type name, validity, whether it supports variables, raw ID, type ID and type data. Part of the engine's debug tools.

label: Inspector itself
summary: A function on the scope inspector of the debug tools that, going by its name, hands back the inspector itself.
details: Vanilla never names it on this type. Self appears often after other types; those lines are only a hint. The game documents no return type.

label: Access editor itself
summary: A function on the debug tools' script object editor that, going by its name, hands back the editor itself.
details: Vanilla never names it on this type; PdxGuiWidget.AccessSelf is a different type and only a hint. The game documents no return type.

label: Value as yes/no
summary: The edited value read as yes or no.
details: Part of the engine's debug editor for a script value (in the object explorer). Vanilla binds the editor's check box to it, shown only when the value is a yes/no value (IsBool); ToggleBool flips it.

label: Value as text
summary: The edited value written out as text.
details: Part of the engine's debug editor for a script value. Vanilla shows it in an editable text box for numbers and flags (SetFromString takes the edit), and read-only next to the ID for a reference to a game object.

label: Reference ID
summary: The ID of the game object the edited value refers to.
details: Part of the engine's debug editor for a script value. Vanilla shows it in a text box with the tooltip "The ID of the reference" when the value is a reference; SetIDFromString takes an edit.

label: Selected type
summary: Which type is chosen in the debug editor's value type drop-down.
details: Part of the engine's debug editor for a script value. Vanilla gives it as the drop-down's selected entry (selectedindex); the list comes from GetVariableTypes. It returns a pair of whole numbers; what each stands for is not documented.

label: Type data
summary: The optional extra type data of the edited value, as text.
details: Part of the engine's debug editor for a script value. Vanilla shows it in a small text box whose tooltip calls type data optional extra data that further sets a scope apart in a few cases; SetTypeDataFromString takes an edit.

label: Value
summary: Going by its name, the edited value as text.
details: Part of the debug tools' script object editor. Vanilla never names it on this type; GetValue is common after variables (Var('name').GetValue) and those lines are only a hint.

label: Value types
summary: The list of value types the debug editor offers in its type drop-down.
details: Part of the engine's debug editor for a script value. Each entry shows its name through ScopeObjectType.GetName; choosing one calls SetSelectedType. The game documents no return type.

label: Is yes/no
summary: Whether the edited value is a yes/no value.
details: Part of the engine's debug editor for a script value; vanilla shows the yes/no check box only when this is yes.

label: Is flag
summary: Whether the edited value is a flag (a word such as `flag:name`).
details: Part of the engine's debug editor for a script value; vanilla shows the editable text box when the value is a number or a flag.

label: Is number
summary: Whether the edited value is a number.
details: Part of the engine's debug editor for a script value; vanilla shows the editable text box when the value is a number or a flag.

label: Is reference
summary: Whether the edited value refers to a game object (a character, title and so on).
details: Part of the engine's debug editor for a script value; when yes, vanilla shows the object as read-only text and its ID in an editable box.

label: Editor itself
summary: A function on the debug tools' script object editor that, going by its name, hands back the editor itself.
details: Vanilla never names it on this type. Self appears often after other types; those lines are only a hint. The game documents no return type.

label: Set from text
summary: Sets the edited value from the text typed into the debug editor's box.
details: Vanilla calls it when editing of the number or flag text box is finished. It takes no argument (the text comes from the box) and returns nothing.

label: Set ID from text
summary: Sets which game object the edited value refers to, from the ID typed into the debug editor.
details: Vanilla calls it when editing of the reference's ID box is finished. Returns nothing.

label: Set value type
summary: Makes the debug editor use the value type chosen in its drop-down.
details: Vanilla calls it when the selection in the type drop-down changes. Returns nothing.

label: Set type data
summary: Sets the edited value's optional type data from the text typed into the debug editor.
details: Vanilla calls it when editing of the type data box is finished. Returns nothing.

label: Toggle yes/no
summary: Flips the edited yes/no value.
details: Vanilla calls it when the debug editor's check box is clicked. Returns nothing.

label: Access provider itself
summary: A function on the debug tools' script object search that, going by its name, hands back the search itself.
details: Vanilla never names it on this type; PdxGuiWidget.AccessSelf is a different type and only a hint. The game documents no return type.

label: Query error
summary: The error message of the object explorer's trigger query.
details: The object explorer, an engine debug tool, filters its list of objects by a trigger typed in. Vanilla shows "Failure: ..." with this text when HasError is yes.

label: Matching objects
summary: How many objects match the object explorer's trigger query.
details: Vanilla shows "X of Y match query", with this as X and GetTotalResultCount as Y.

label: Total objects
summary: How many objects the object explorer's query looks through in all.
details: Vanilla shows "X of Y match query", with this as Y and GetFilteredResultCount as X.

label: Query trigger
summary: The trigger text the object explorer uses as its query.
details: Vanilla shows it in the multi-line query text box; SetTriggerString takes an edit.

label: Has query error
summary: Whether the object explorer's trigger query failed.
details: Vanilla shows the error line ("Failure: " with GetError) only when this is yes.

label: Provider itself
summary: A function on the debug tools' script object search that, going by its name, hands back the search itself.
details: Vanilla never names it on this type. Self appears often after other types; those lines are only a hint. The game documents no return type.

label: Set query trigger
summary: Stores the trigger text typed into the object explorer's query box.
details: Vanilla calls it when editing the box is finished or Return is pressed (then also UpdateFilter). It takes no argument and returns nothing.

label: Apply query
summary: Applies the object explorer's trigger query again, so the list matches it.
details: Vanilla calls it from the "Apply" button and on Return in the query box, together with a request to update the list. Returns nothing.

label: Access object type itself
summary: A function on a script object type entry that, going by its name, hands back the entry itself.
details: Vanilla never names it on this type; PdxGuiWidget.AccessSelf is a different type and only a hint. The game documents no return type.

label: Type name
summary: The name of a value type in the debug editor's type drop-down.
details: Vanilla shows it as the text of each entry in the drop-down filled from ScopeObjectEditor.GetVariableTypes.

label: Object type itself
summary: A function on a script object type entry that, going by its name, hands back the entry itself.
details: Vanilla never names it on this type. Self appears often after other types; those lines are only a hint. The game documents no return type.

label: Access profiler entry itself
summary: A function on a row of the script profiler (the debug tool that measures how long script takes) that, going by its name, hands back the row itself.
details: Vanilla never names it on this type; PdxGuiWidget.AccessSelf is a different type and only a hint. The game documents no return type.

label: Average own time
summary: Going by its name, the average time one run of this script piece took, not counting the script it calls.
details: Part of the script profiler, a debug tool. Exclusive means without the time of nested script, going by the usual meaning in profilers. The unit is not documented. Vanilla never uses it.

label: Average total time
summary: Going by its name, the average time one run of this script piece took, including the script it calls.
details: Part of the script profiler, a debug tool. The unit is not documented. Vanilla never uses it.

label: Call count
summary: Going by its name, how many times this script piece ran while the profiler measured.
details: Part of the script profiler, a debug tool. Vanilla never uses it.

label: Script file
summary: Going by its name, the script file this profiler row comes from.
details: Part of the script profiler, a debug tool. The game documents no return type; GetFileName gives the name. Vanilla never uses it.

label: File and line
summary: Going by its name, the script file and line number of this profiler row, as text.
details: Part of the script profiler, a debug tool. How it differs from GetFileNameAndLine (perhaps the full path against the bare name) is not documented. Vanilla never uses it.

label: File name
summary: Going by its name, the name of the script file this profiler row comes from.
details: Part of the script profiler, a debug tool. The game documents no return type. Vanilla never uses it.

label: File name and line
summary: Going by its name, the script file's name and the line number of this profiler row, as text.
details: Part of the script profiler, a debug tool. Vanilla never uses it.

label: Timing text
summary: The measured time of this script profiler entry, written out for display.
details: The script profiler is an engine debug tool that measures how long script takes. Vanilla shows it next to each caller and callee in the call graph and as the current entry's "Timing", only when the entry has samples.

label: Line number
summary: Going by its name, the line in the script file where this profiled piece starts.
details: Part of the script profiler, a debug tool. Vanilla never uses it.

label: Longest total time
summary: Going by its name, the longest time a single run of this script piece took, including the script it calls.
details: Part of the script profiler, a debug tool. The unit is not documented. Vanilla never uses it.

label: Shortest total time
summary: Going by its name, the shortest time a single run of this script piece took, including the script it calls.
details: Part of the script profiler, a debug tool. The unit is not documented. Vanilla never uses it.

label: Own time per frame
summary: Going by its name, how much time this script piece takes per drawn frame, not counting the script it calls.
details: Part of the script profiler, a debug tool. The unit is not documented. Vanilla never uses it.

label: Total time per frame
summary: Going by its name, how much time this script piece takes per drawn frame, including the script it calls.
details: Part of the script profiler, a debug tool. The unit is not documented. Vanilla never uses it.

label: Own time per tick
summary: Going by its name, how much time this script piece takes per game tick (one step of game time), not counting the script it calls.
details: Part of the script profiler, a debug tool. The unit is not documented. Vanilla never uses it.

label: Total time per tick
summary: Going by its name, how much time this script piece takes per game tick, including the script it calls.
details: Part of the script profiler, a debug tool. The unit is not documented. Vanilla never uses it.

label: Short description
summary: A short text naming this script profiler entry.
details: Vanilla shows it as the name of each caller and callee in the profiler's call graph, and of the current entry.

label: Timing
summary: Going by its name, this profiler row's measured time as a number.
details: Part of the script profiler, a debug tool. Which of the measured times it is (total, average or per frame) is not documented. Vanilla never uses it.

label: Total own time
summary: Going by its name, all the time this script piece took while measured, not counting the script it calls.
details: Part of the script profiler, a debug tool. The unit is not documented. Vanilla never uses it.

label: Total time
summary: Going by its name, all the time this script piece took while measured, including the script it calls.
details: Part of the script profiler, a debug tool. The unit is not documented. Vanilla never uses it.

label: Entry type
summary: Going by its name, the kind of script this profiler row measures (for example an effect or a trigger), as text.
details: Part of the script profiler, a debug tool. Vanilla never names it on this type; the GetType lines follow other types (task contracts, situations) and are only a hint.

label: Variant
summary: Going by its name, a variant label of this profiler row, as text.
details: Part of the script profiler, a debug tool. What the variant stands for is not documented. Vanilla never uses it.

label: Has file location
summary: Going by its name, whether this profiler row knows which script file and line it comes from.
details: Part of the script profiler, a debug tool. Vanilla never uses it.

label: Has samples
summary: Whether the script profiler recorded any measurements for this entry.
details: Vanilla shows the entry's timing, and for the current entry the call count, only when this is yes.

label: Open in code editor
summary: Going by its name, opens this row's script file in an outside code editor.
details: Part of the script profiler, a debug tool; it returns nothing. Vanilla never uses it.

label: Open in script editor
summary: Going by its name, opens this row's script in the game's own script editor tool.
details: Part of the script profiler, a debug tool; it returns nothing. Vanilla never uses it.

label: Select entry
summary: Makes this entry the current one in the script profiler's call graph.
details: Vanilla calls it when a caller or callee row is clicked. Returns nothing.

label: Select file
summary: Going by its name, selects the script file of this profiler row.
details: Part of the script profiler, a debug tool; it returns nothing. Vanilla never uses it.

label: Profiler entry itself
summary: A function on a script profiler row that, going by its name, hands back the row itself.
details: Vanilla never names it on this type. Self appears often after other types; those lines are only a hint. The game documents no return type.

label: Access file line itself
summary: A function on a file-and-line row of the script profiler that, going by its name, hands back the row itself.
details: Vanilla never names it on this type; PdxGuiWidget.AccessSelf is a different type and only a hint. The game documents no return type.

label: Average own time
summary: Going by its name, the average time one run of the script at this file line took, not counting the script it calls.
details: Part of the script profiler, a debug tool that groups its timings by file and line here. The unit is not documented. Vanilla never uses it.

label: Average total time
summary: Going by its name, the average time one run of the script at this file line took, including the script it calls.
details: Part of the script profiler, a debug tool. The unit is not documented. Vanilla never uses it.

label: Call count
summary: Going by its name, how many times the script at this file line ran while the profiler measured.
details: Part of the script profiler, a debug tool. Vanilla never uses it.

label: Timing text
summary: The measured time of the script at this file line, written out for display.
details: Vanilla shows it in the script profiler's file view, only when the line has samples.
